scenes.title: Pushed a secret by mistake?
scenes.body: 1) **Revoke the key now** in the provider's console. 2) Create a new key in your `.env`. 3) Remove the file and add it to `.gitignore`. Deleting it in a new commit is **not** enough: it is still in the history, and bots scan GitHub for keys within minutes.

items.q: What is the difference between Git and GitHub?
items.a: **Git** is the version control tool that runs on your computer: commits, history, branches. **GitHub** is a website that hosts Git repositories and adds collaboration: pull requests, reviews, issues.
items.trap: Saying they are the same thing, or that you need GitHub to use Git.

items.a: `add` moves changes into the **staging area** (choose what goes in). `commit` saves the staged snapshot in the **local** history with a message. `push` sends your commits to the **remote**, like GitHub.
items.trap: Thinking `commit` uploads your work. Until you push, it exists only on your laptop.

items.q: You committed an API key and pushed it. What do you do?
items.a: **Revoke the key immediately** and issue a new one; then remove the file, add it to `.gitignore`, and if needed clean the history. Revoking comes first because the key must be treated as already stolen.
items.trap: "I deleted the file in the next commit." The key is still in the history.

items.a: When two branches change **the same lines** differently, Git can't choose for you. It marks both versions in the file; you edit it to the right result, then `add` and `commit`.
items.trap: Panicking, or deleting and re-cloning. A conflict is normal: read both sides, keep the right code.

scenes.question: You edited `app.py`. In which order do these commands put it on GitHub?
scenes.explain: Stage the change (`add`), save it in the local history (`commit`), then send the commits to the remote (`push`).

scenes.question: `.env` is listed in `.gitignore`. What does `git status` show for it?
options: Nothing: ignored files are not listed
scenes.explain: Ignored files don't appear in `git status`. Check why a file is ignored with `git check-ignore -v .env`.

scenes.question: A teammate pushed new commits. Which command brings them into your local `main`?
scenes.explain: `pull` fetches new commits from the remote and merges them. `clone` is only for getting a repository the first time.
